questions.q: What is a Date Part in Tableau?
options: A date broken into a cyclical component, like 'Month,' where every occurrence (May 2022, May 2023, ...) is grouped together regardless of year
The exact, ungrouped, row-level date value
A date field that has been converted to a string
A date with the time component removed
questions.explain: Date Parts aggregate to a specific cyclical component of a date — 'Month' as a date part lumps every May together across all years, ignoring the year entirely.

questions.q: What is a Date Value in Tableau, and how does it differ from a Date Part?
options: A date truncated to a level but still anchored to its real calendar position, so 'Month' produces a separate bucket for each actual month-year combination
The same thing as a Date Part, just with a different label in the menu
A date value is always the exact, untruncated date
Date Values only exist for the Year level
questions.explain: Unlike a Date Part, a Date Value stays tied to its real position in the calendar — 'Month' as a date value gives you May 2022 as a distinct bucket from May 2023.

questions.q: If you put 'Month' on Columns as a Date Part with three years of data, how many column headers do you get?
options: 12 — one for each month, with all years combined into each
36 — one for each month of each year
3 — one for each year
1 — all months combined into a single column
questions.explain: Date Parts ignore the year, so 'Month' as a date part always produces exactly 12 buckets (January-December) no matter how many years of data are behind it.

questions.q: What does Exact Date give you, and what's its closest SQL equivalent?
options: The full, row-level, untruncated date — equivalent to selecting the raw date column with no function applied
The date rounded to the nearest month
Only the year portion of the date
A random sample of dates from the data source
questions.explain: Exact Date is the most granular option — the untouched original date value, just like selecting the raw date column in a SQL query with no DATEPART or truncation function applied.

questions.q: You want a chart that shows how sales trended continuously from month to month over several years, without months from different years being merged together. Which should you choose?
options: Month as a Date Value
Month as a Date Part
Year as a Date Part
Exact Date is the only option that works for this
questions.explain: Month as a Date Value keeps each month anchored to its actual year, producing a continuously growing timeline (May 2022, June 2022, ... May 2023) rather than lumping same-named months from different years together.
